auth.keyHelp: In IAM open the read-only user, choose Security credentials, then Create access key and pick Other; the secret is shown only once.

read.label: List EC2 instances in the region
Get cost and usage by service for a date range
Show which AWS identity the key belongs to

tested: mock; real service refused a fake key
notes: AWS has no bearer token: every request must be signed with Signature Version 4 from the access key ID, secret and region (the Authorization header value is computed per request, not pasted). The format has no multi-host concept, so each action here carries its own host, signing service name and protocol. Test call: STS GetCallerIdentity, a form POST to / with body Action=GetCallerIdentity&Version=2011-06-15, which needs no IAM permission and returns Arn, UserId and Account (the XML Arn is the 'who'). STS docs recommend the regional endpoint sts.<region>.amazonaws.com over the legacy global sts.amazonaws.com. EC2 DescribeInstances is a Query API call: Action=DescribeInstances, Version=2016-11-15 against ec2.<region>.amazonaws.com, per-region, XML response, paginate with MaxResults and NextToken (MaxResults cannot be combined with InstanceId.N). Cost Explorer is a JSON 1.1 call to the single endpoint https://ce.us-east-1.amazonaws.com with header X-Amz-Target: AWSInsightsIndexService.GetCostAndUsage and body TimePeriod {Start,End as YYYY-MM-DD, end exclusive}, Granularity (DAILY, MONTHLY or HOURLY), Metrics (e.g. UnblendedCost), optional GroupBy such as {Type DIMENSION, Key SERVICE}. The signing service name for Cost Explorer ('ce') is not printed on the pages I read; it is the same short name the API uses in its SDK id (ce-2017-10-25), so verify before relying on it. The user must have Cost Explorer enabled, and the docs only say AWS charges apply (see AWS Cost Management Pricing). How to make a read-only IAM user: in the IAM console choose Users > Create user, no console access needed, then Set permissions > Attach policies directly and pick the AWS managed policy ReadOnlyAccess (arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/ReadOnlyAccess). Its JSON includes ec2:Describe* and ec2:Get*, and lists individual Cost Explorer reads such as ce:GetCostAndUsage and ce:GetCostForecast, so one policy covers all three calls here. Then open the user's Security credentials tab > Create access key > Other and copy the secret, which is shown once. Do not attach any write policy; no write actions are listed for this reason. IAM best practice in the docs prefers federation or roles over long-term user keys; an IAM user key is the only form this connection uses. Official MCP server: AWS MCP Server, managed remote, https://aws-mcp.us-east-1.api.aws/mcp (also us-west-2, ap-southeast-1, ap-southeast-2, ap-northeast-1, eu-central-1, eu-west-1, eu-west-2), authenticates by OAuth (attach AWSMCPSignInOAuthAccessPolicy) or by SigV4 through the MCP Proxy for AWS; SigV4 mode also allows a read-only mode that hides write tools.
